newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain-Soy basis offers up, Corn steady.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain-Soy basis offers up, Corn steady.

text.p: FOB Gulf soybean basis offers rose three to four cents a bushel bolstered by forecasts for wet weather in the U.S. Midwest which would slow soybean and corn harvesting while corn basis were mostly steady.
Soft red winter wheat values sagged on a lack of export activity, one dealer said.
Dealers cited a lack of nearby farmer selling, harvest delays and possible logistical problems on the river system sparked by the adverse weather.
In export news, South Korean feed mill companies on Tuesday bought 52,500 tonnes of U.S. No.3 yellow corn from Japanese trading house Mitsubishi.

The feed mill companies bought the corn at 87.95 cents per bushel over CBOT March futures if from the Pacific Northwest or at 85.95 cents over March if from U.S. Gulf. Shipment was set at seller's option for February 14-March 5 if from Pacific Northwest or for Feb 1-20 if from the U.S. Gulf.
